doc.title: Chazz Frichtel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 13, 2016

title: Mangione's music and the demands of the book
summary: The first rehearsals at SIR; mix of charts and written lines, with bebop, Latin and orchestra dates, bass features and singing.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: Yes, in New York. Studio Instrument Rental rehearsal space.
And did he have like chord charts or did he have lines for you?

It was a combination of both. He had certain things that were very specific parts, but most of the tunes were kind of basic chord charts with certain lines written in. And what was great about that gig for me was that after all these years of playing in more of a pop — with singers per se. With Chuck’s band you had to understand bebop, Latin, we did certain orchestra dates so you had to kind of be able to play the orchestra book. And for me it was a blowing gig. There were several bass features and I started — I took over, Charles was the singer — Charles Meeks was the singer, so I kind of took over the singing role as well. And it was really fun. And before I did that gig I really did a lot of shedding because I thought wow, it required more from me than a lot of the other gigs had. And it was really, really fun, really fun. And it was a different vocabulary, different sensibility, new jokes, you know. It was wonderful.
